_about: Named viewer settings (not to be confused with the repo root's capture_presets.json, which holds capture settings for the Python pipeline). Each key is a panel control's id and the value it is set to, exactly as if the slider had been moved by hand. 'reliefscale': 'grid' means match the grid size. Keys about the preset itself: 'short' is the button's text and 'label' its tooltip; 'view' presses a camera button; 'camera' frames a shot (azimuth and elevation in degrees, distance in tiles); 'research' shows the button only in Research mode; 'chapter' makes it a story step instead of a button, with 'caption' shown over the canvas ({tiles}, {size}, {world}, {scene}, {source}, {collects}, {exposed} are filled in from the tileset). Add your own; the viewer lists whatever is here.

river.label: The river world: Lütschine gravel along the water, Uruguay grass on the banks, a 6 m river cut into the valley.

heights.label: Material by altitude alone, no region filter.

plain.label: The capture alone: no terrain, no rule, no far field. For scenes that are not ground tiles.

proof-on.label: Rule on, flat light, survey view: the on/off figure.

ch1.label: Tiles of ground, close up, outlined.
ch1.caption: 1 · capture Each outlined square is one tile: {size} of {source}, rebuilt so that its four edges can meet other tiles. Everything that follows is built from {tiles} of these.

ch2.label: Wang tiles and their edge colours.
ch2.caption: 2 · tiles Wang tiles. Each edge carries a colour (the bands); a tile sits only next to tiles whose touching edge has the same colour, so any layout is continuous and needs no search. A tile keeps only a frame along its edges; its middle is a centre drawn per cell from a pool of the capture's own ground, so the same tile is never repeated whole.

ch3.label: The tiles laid over terrain, materials at random.
ch3.caption: 3 · world The same {tiles} tiles over generated, eroded terrain, {world} across, continued to the horizon by the far field. Each cell's material is chosen at random: the baseline.

ch4.label: The same world with materials placed by the land.
ch4.caption: 4 · rule Each material placed from the terrain: {collects} collects in hollows and channels, {exposed} stays on steep, convex ground. Computed from drainage, position, slope and height rather than painted. Compare with step 3, or turn on show the decision under materials.

river1.label: Tiles of ground, close up, outlined.
river1.caption: 1 · capture Each outlined square is one tile: {size} of real ground, gravel from a drone survey of the Lütschine and grass from a flight over Uruguayan grassland, each trained as Gaussian splats and rebuilt so its four edges can meet other tiles.

river2.label: Wang tiles and their edge colours.
river2.caption: 2 · tiles Wang tiles. Each edge carries a colour (the bands); a tile sits only next to tiles whose touching edge has the same colour, so any layout is continuous and needs no search. A tile keeps only a frame along its edges; its middle is a centre drawn per cell from a pool of the capture's own ground, so the same tile is never repeated whole.

river3.label: The tiles over a valley with its river, materials at random.
river3.caption: 3 · world The tiles over a generated valley, {world} across. Where the valley drains, a river is cut into it in metres: a bed deeper on the outside of bends, pools and riffles every few widths, and a level surface whose colour and ripples are layers measured from the drone photos. Materials here are at random: the baseline.

river4.label: The same valley with materials placed by the land and the river.
river4.caption: 4 · rule Materials placed by the land and the river: gravel bars lie low beside the water and within reach of it, wide on flat floors and thin under steep banks, and grass takes the higher ground. Compare with step 3.
